facts.raw_span: A 59-year-old Japanese man presented with malaise and chills that began the day before his visit
Medical history included hypertension and hyperlipidemia
he was diagnosed with acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL)
On day 10 of hospitalization, he experienced a 40.2°C fever
Percussion tenderness in the right upper quadrant
Leukocyte count 0.1 × 10⁹/L (50% neutrophils)
Alkaline phosphatase 1065 U/L
Multiple, small, circumscribed, hypoattenuating lesions in the liver and spleen
Blood cultures: Positive for yeast after 30 hours
Gram staining: Revealed arthroconidia and hyphal fungi
Molecular identification: D1/D2 26S rDNA and internal transcribed spacer region of rRNA gene analysis performed
Drug susceptibility testing: MIC values - voriconazole 0.25 μg/mL, micafungin 4.0 μg/mL

support_spans: Blood cultures: Positive for yeast after 30 hours
Gram staining: Revealed arthroconidia and hyphal fungi
Multiple, small, circumscribed, hypoattenuating lesions in the liver and spleen
concepts.why: The presence of arthroconidia and hyphal fungi in Gram staining and the hypoattenuating lesions in the liver and spleen are unusual findings that suggest Invasive Aspergillosis.

contradict_spans: Gram staining: Revealed arthroconidia and hyphal fungi

contradict_spans: Gram staining: Revealed arthroconidia and hyphal fungi

support_spans: Blood cultures: Positive for yeast after 30 hours
Gram staining: Revealed arthroconidia and hyphal fungi
concepts.why: The presence of arthroconidia and hyphal fungi in Gram staining and the positive blood culture for yeast could suggest Fusariosis.
The patient's low leukocyte count, molecular identification of fungal infection, and drug susceptibility testing results explain the diagnosis of Hepatosplenic Candidiasis.
